A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MambaPEFT work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original vision and commonsense-reasoning experiments, including PEFT benchmarks, ablations, and HybridPEFT search results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds results for LoRA applied to individual Pythia modules in Table 6.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same Affix-tuning, Partial LoRA, Partial-tuning regularization, Additional-scan initialization, and HybridPEFT search procedures. The added comparison uses existing LoRA configurations without revising the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 19 VTAB-1k tasks and eight commonsense-reasoning tasks, retaining the appendix data-size experiments. The new module comparison uses existing language benchmarks without adding task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 6 adds Pythia comparators applying LoRA separately to query_key_value, dense_4h_to_h, dense_h_to_4h, and dense. v2 Table 3 reports only full fine-tuning and combined-module LoRA for Pythia. Newly discussed SDLoRA is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Table 6 introduces one-module-at-a-time Pythia controls alongside combined-module LoRA at the four retained model sizes. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. The Mamba full-tuning learning rate of 5e-5 moves from Appendix B.1 prose into Table 8; this is not a changed setting.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a targeted analysis of whether concentrating LoRA on individual modules behaves differently in Pythia and Mamba. Table 6 supplies new Pythia module ablations alongside previously reported Mamba results. Earlier sensitivity, initialization, data-size, and model-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for these experiments. The added results continue the existing practice of reporting point accuracies.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds 16 Pythia module-specific result rows. For example, Pythia 1.4B individual-module average accuracies range from 49.3 to 50.2, versus the retained combined-module LoRA score of 50.5. Previously reported tables retain their values; repeated Mamba rows and recolored curves are not new results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the Additional-scan derivation, and Appendix B.2 search-space reasoning are unchanged. The new discussion of Prefix-tuning expressiveness adds no formal assumptions, theorem, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: comprehensive Mamba PEFT exploration, Mamba-specific adaptations, effective method combinations, and advantages relative to Transformers. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly interprets the module comparison as showing different LoRA-placement preferences across architectures. New Appendix A.8 argues that arbitrary Affix-tuning insertion avoids the cited Prefix-tuning expressiveness limitation. Existing applicability limitations and future-work qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 promises code release after publication; v3 states that source code is available and provides a concrete repository link in the abstract. Existing implementation details remain substantively unchanged, including the full-tuning learning rate redistributed into the settings table.

R1.justification: v3 adds Galim et al. (2024) and Appendix A.8 on concurrent SDLoRA work, distinguishing its selective channel/state updates from this paper's benchmarking focus and discussing Prefix-tuning limitations. This is a localized positioning addition.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. v3 makes small wording edits, adds acknowledgements and a concurrent-work subsection, extends Appendix A.4, and renumbers the existing future-work subsection from A.8 to A.9.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 6, revises colors, markers, and legends in Figures 6–7, and adds a Full row to the learning-rate table using information previously stated in prose. Later tables are renumbered and repositioned, while existing scientific displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Pythia controls strengthen evidence for the architecture comparison, while the concurrent-work discussion and concrete code location improve context and reproducibility information. These are limited gains around unchanged methods and established results. Some qualifications remain necessary: the new Mamba interpretation overgeneralizes mixed in_proj results, and the main text still calls SLL LoRA the only Mamba PEFT work despite acknowledging SDLoRA in Appendix A.8. The additions nevertheless provide a modest net improvement.
